title: Autonomous Parameter Surgery: How LLMs Implant Selective Backdoors into Language Models
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext; main text, tables 1-3, limitations; appendices not read in detail)
why_wsp: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, in a restricted workspace (metered GPU probes, tagged linear algebra, rank-update/set_rows/replace write ops), turns a plain-text backdoor rule into gradient-free weight edits of a separate LM, iterating against dev and hidden-verification feedback.
domain: LLM backdoor implantation (sentiment classification on IMDb/Yelp)
target: Qwen3.5-0.8B (24 blocks), Llama-3.2-1B (16 blocks; 1.24B scalars), SmolLM3-3B (36 blocks)
interface: code/tensor tools (restricted JSON algebra graph with origin tags; write ops rank_update, set_rows, replace)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (avg 46.3 turns, 3.8 candidate revisions; hidden verification gate)
self_editing: no; editor modifies separate target models
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "a single neuron edit on Llama-3.2-1B that modifies only 6,144 parameters (0.0005% of the model)" (Sec 1); dense S-I2 edit "22.47M of 22.54M entries modified" of one down_proj (Sec 6.3)

headline_results.quote: the modified checkpoints reach 99.2% mean attack success on the editing domain and 97.6% transfer success on the unseen domain
The average across seven multiple-choice tasks shifts by +0.07 pp ... IFEval strict accuracy shifts by −0.44 pp, GSM8K flexible accuracy by −0.91 pp, and GSM8K strict accuracy by −1.69 pp
the LLM places its final intervention in the last transformer block in 17 of 18 runs
initial edits leak 24.7–54.5 pp onto neighboring triggers; iterative GPU feedback cuts drift to 3.5–3.8 pp at 98.5%–99.8% ASR
across all 18 runs, 171 of 436 algebra calls fail and roll back before the editor refines its calculation
Edits learned on narrower Yelp reviews keep high trigger activation on IMDb (Yelp → IMDb: 97.03% ASR) but suffer larger boundary drift (8.75–10.50 pp)
dense updates shift a tensor’s norm by as little as 0.29%–0.54%

cost.quote: runs average 46.3 turns, 16.5 minutes on a single consumer GPU, and $1.74 in API fees ($31.34 across all 18 runs

baselines_and_controls: Base checkpoints; five control conditions (clean, body marker, §§, §., § §) with directional error tracking; unseen-domain transfer; 7 MC benchmarks, WikiText-2 PPL, GSM8K, IFEval. Explicitly no human-designed editing baselines (BadEdit, SteerEdit) run.
runs_and_variance: 3 independent sessions per model-domain pair (18 total); mean ± sd over 3 runs per cell reported in Table 2.
robustness_of_edits: Persistence tested by fresh-process reload with editor removed; domain transfer tested. No fine-tuning, quantization or defense robustness tests.
verification: Hidden 256-item verification gate before submission; content-hashed checkpoints; trace auditing; statistical confirmation on ~4,000 reviews per domain. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Workspace blocks CPU simulation by tagging tensor origin; authors cannot rule out prior exposure to architectures, but cite probing across depths, varied layer choices and 171/436 rolled-back algebra calls as "pointing to active localization rather than static recall".
limitations_stated: Single editor model at low effort; no human-designed editing baselines in same harness; only two English sentiment datasets with fixed template/trigger; possible prior editor exposure to public targets; artifacts (checkpoints, prompts, updates) withheld.
code_or_data: none found (authors withhold modified checkpoints, raw prompts and weight updates)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, 2026)
notes_for_survey: Closed-loop WSP backdoor implantation with a cheap editor ($1.74/run) and a sandbox that prevents CPU-side simulation of edits; edits are selective against near-miss triggers and transfer across domains. Edits leave standard benchmarks and weight-norm statistics nearly unchanged; artifacts withheld.
